prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: mobile-first web app composition comp, portrait iPhone screen
Primary request: high-fidelity shippable Open Calory Tracker daily log using the already chosen polished category-standard visual world, with Apple Health as the quality reference for native iPhone hierarchy, privacy, restrained surfaces, typography, and information clarity. This is composition option 2: a pinned daily summary rather than a large dashboard grid.
Structure: iOS-like navigation title “Food Log” with a small PRIVATE indicator and Settings; compact horizontal date strip; a large pinned calorie highlight showing 1,420 of 2,050 kcal with a thin neutral progress track; below it an inset grouped nutrition list with Protein, Carbohydrate, Fat and a second-page cue; chronological Food Entries as a clean grouped list with times and disclosure chevrons; water summary with 8, 16, 24 fl oz quick actions; a thumb-reachable green Add Food button and modest Add Water action; bottom tabs Log, History, Settings.
Subject/content: Saturday, August 29; Today; Mock data; 1,420 / 2,050 kcal; 630 kcal remaining; Protein 72 / 120 g; Carbohydrate 131 / 230 g; Fat 44 / 70 g; Greek yogurt with blueberries 320 kcal at 8:12 AM; Turkey & avocado sandwich 540 kcal at 12:36 PM; Water 40 / 80 fl oz; Fiber Incomplete; USDA FoodData Central attribution.
Style/medium: realistic polished mobile product UI, not concept art, not a phone mockup. Cool near-white ground, white inset grouped surfaces, deep slate text, fresh green only for actionable elements, pale blue secondary data, system-like humanist sans, precise tabular numerals, minimal shadows, restrained separators, no decorative illustration.
Composition/framing: full portrait 9:16 viewport without device frame; first viewport emphasizes daily comprehension and then logging; generous Apple-quality alignment and optical spacing; no oversized greeting.
Constraints: English; practical WCAG-conscious hierarchy; neutral nonjudgmental progress; no food photos or illustrations, no gamification, no streaks, no badges, no medical claims, no advertisements, no premium upsells, no fake logos, no watermark; render provided labels accurately and do not invent claims.
